en: The Prophecy of the Extinction of the Semblance Dharma of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, translated by the State Preceptor, Tripitaka Master, and Śramaṇa Facheng. It was brought from the Kingdom of Khotan.
Six generations of kings have already passed, and it has reached the seventh generation of kings, whose name is:
During the reign of Viśākha, there was a monastery in that country.
It is named Sāgaramahānada. Not far from this monastery,
there is a mountain valley named Sākajīna.
In those mountain valleys there was an arhat,
who had a bhikṣu as his disciple;
[the disciple] followed his teacher.
Having trained in the monastic discipline (*vinaya*),
he later encountered the *Candragarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra* as well as the holy teachings.
He then asked the venerable Arhat:
"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
[what became of] Khotan, Śule, and Anxi?"
How long will the Tathāgata’s semblance Dharma, stūpas,
and so forth remain in the world?
Who shall destroy them?
"Where exactly does it reach?
I pray that you will explain this for me.
At that time, the Arhat immediately said: "After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni..."
Those images of the Dharma and the stupas shall remain in the world for two thousand years,
after which they will perish and disappear.
The three kingdoms of Khotan and so forth;
the Han, the Red-faced, the Suvī, the Turks,
and the Uyghur rebels.
They brandished their weapons and came to invade and inflict damage;
consequently, the Buddha-dharma gradually declined and was destroyed,
and stupas and monasteries were demolished.
The provisions and requisites for the Saṃgha were also completely cut off.
Within these three kingdoms,
the Anxi and Shule regions ceased the practice of the Dharma as they were invaded by bandits.
Consequently, they harassed the stupas and monasteries;
for the most part, they were burned down,
and all were utterly destroyed.
The various monasteries were abandoned,
and most of the monks moved to the kingdom of Khotan;
[they settled] in the stupas and monasteries of Khotan.
Five hundred bodhisattvas constantly protect and uphold [this teaching];
thus, two hundred and fifty follow the monastic code,
while two hundred and fifty remain among the laity.
Receiving birth and providing protection,
this Niu-tou Mountain Temple shall always be trodden by the one thousand five hundred Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa.
They took it as their palace.
Because the various worthies and sages have empowered the wondrous Dharma of the Khotan stūpas and temples through their majestic virtue and compassion,
those who practice the Dharma are more numerous here than in other countries.
He remained in the world for a long time.
At that time, various kings and others engaged in tumultuous strife and conflict because they desired to seize the kingdom of Khotan.
Whichever king obtains it shall become a great donor for Khotan,
ensuring that [the Dharma] is neither defiled nor extinguished.
One should always make offerings.
At that time, King Crimson Face possessed great majesty and power.
They extensively invaded other countries and annexed them as their own territory.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva.
He was born in the Land of Red Faces and,
as king within his own realm, widely practiced the sublime Dharma.
From another country...
He invited that Dharma Master and his collection of sutras and śāstras;
then, within the Land of Red Faces,
he established a vihāra.
He constructed stūpas and delivered the multitudes of sentient beings,
including kings, ministers, and all the people of the land.
He widely practiced the True Dharma.
At that time, Khotan was subject to that King of the Red Face;
therefore, he widely practiced the True Dharma.
He established stūpas and monasteries,
assigned households, fields, and gardens to the Three Jewels,
and performed great offerings.
The King of Crimson Face has practiced the sublime for seven generations;
these are the kings of those seven generations.
In other countries, regarding all places where the Triple Gem and stūpas and temples are located,
they do not give rise to evil thoughts,
nor do they cause harm.
At that time, among the monastic community of Khotan,
as described in the *Candragarbha-bodhisattva-vyākaraṇa-sūtra*,
for the most part, their faith gradually became thin.
One does not seek worldly profit or fame through the precepts and Dharma,
nor does one enter into the secret deliberations of kings and ministers.
This will cause the True Dharma to gradually decline and waste away;
at that time, the king, his ministers, and their descendants will lose their pure faith.
All items that are permanently maintained shall be used by the bhikṣus for their own needs; however,
the property belonging to the temples and monasteries of Khotan where the True Dharma permanently resides shall remain as such.
It is not as it was in former days;
it will gradually decline and waste away.
The kings and great ministers—
He felt no joy toward the community of renunciants.
Later, at another time, there was a bodhisattva who was the seventh-generation king of the country of Red Face.
That king took Princess Han Pusa as his consort.
The queen, accompanied by six hundred attendants, arrived in the kingdom of Crimson Face.
At that time, the princess was profoundly devoted to the Buddha-dharma.
He possesses great merit and virtue;
King Raktamukha also possesses great pure faith,
exceeding that of his predecessors.
The True Dharma was widely propagated. At such a time,
the King of Khotan was young and did not practice the Buddha’s True Dharma.
The elder bhikṣus said:
"It is not so that you should return to lay life;
it is not so that you should follow your own will."
Driven out to another place by that pursuit,
the entire community of monks gathered at the Caṇpā Monastery.
While they were deliberating on this matter before the assembly within the monastery,
seven portions of food made of precious gold suddenly appeared.
At that time, five thousand bhikṣus whose food had been cut off by the king and who were in dire straits exchanged those gold provisions for three months' worth of grain.
Some returned to secular life;
some did not return to secular life;
and some departed for other regions.
Separated from their parents, relatives, kinsmen, and native country,
they were overcome with extreme grief and distress,
running about and weeping aloud.
The assembly of monks proceeded on their way to the monastery of Mu-hung.
There, they found a great stūpa.
There was a great and pure deity, the Śakra-rāja,
who opened that stūpa and brought forth a golden bowl filled to the brim with precious pearls.
He offered them to the community of monks.
Furthermore, there were other lay donors of pure faith who provided various requisites for the assembly.
He gave it to the Saṃgha.
In this manner, the Saṃgha gradually proceeded to the Nulu River,
using those pearls as provisions for half a month's journey.
At that time, the assembly of monks arrived at the Nu-lu River and stayed at the Song-duo-he-gong-niang Temple. Then,
the Heavenly King Vaisravana and Śrī-devī transformed themselves into a husband and wife.
Dwelling there,
they respectfully address the Saṃgha, saying:
"We are performing meritorious deeds."
I pray that you will graciously accept this:
for half a month past, I have established a great assembly of offerings and reverently sustained the Sangha.
The goddess Puṇyavatī took a sleeve from her garment containing gold and precious coins and offered them to the assembly of monks.
At that time, the monastic community traveled together from the country of the Great Red-Faced Barbarians to Mount Bhadra.
Encountering a gatekeeper who detained him and would not let him pass,
he spoke these words:
"There are other roads elsewhere."
"Go as you please.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa transformed his body into that of a white yak with a sore on its back and a rope halter.
When the assembly of monks saw this, they said to one another:
"This ox with the back-wound is a domestic animal of humans.
Where shall we go? We should follow after it."
At that time, the yak led them along a direct path for four or five intervals until all the monks reached the territory of Sābi in the kingdom of Aruṇa.
There, the army of Sābi was stationed at the pass to guard the road, and they encountered the many learned monks arriving from the west.
The King of White and Red Face knew this.
At that time, the king’s consort heard that the great assembly of monks had lost their lands and were scattering in all directions,
and she said to the king:
"I have prepared vehicles for transport and all necessary provisions;
I pray that you will invite the assembly of monks to come to the kingdom of Crimson Face."
The king also granted his permission.
Having prepared the draft animals and vehicles,
he went out to welcome the assembly of monks.
Upon arriving at the Kingdom of Red Faces,
the princess of the King of Red Faces, accompanied by her attendants, made offerings and paid homage.
She then addressed the venerable masters among the assembly of monks who were well-versed in the Tripitaka, saying:
"Are there any others besides you who have fled?
The venerable Tripitaka masters replied respectfully:
"Anxi, Shule, Bo-li, and the kingdom of Jashimi."
There being such a vast multitude of monks scattered and migrating to that place,
he immediately dispatched messengers to invite the assembly of monks to the country of Red Faces.
At that time, seven monasteries were established in the kingdom of Crimson Face (Cimukoku).
Various ritual implements were prepared,
and the number of households providing permanent support for the monasteries became twice as great as it had been in former days.
He established the community of monks so that they resided in seven monasteries.
After three or four years had passed,
a malignant ulcer broke out on the princess's chest.
During her time of illness and suffering,
the princess said to the king:
"I shall not escape this disease."
"I vow to offer all my servants and wealth to the Triple Gem," and the King also granted his permission.
He caused his six hundred attendants to all leave the household life as monastics.
Subsequently, the princess’s life came to its end.
After the princess passed away, [the king]...
Within the realm of King Crimson Face,
an outbreak of bean-pox occurred;
among the ministers, officials, and their sons and grandsons, those who died were numerous.
Then those ministers gathered together and said to the king:
"Within the borders of Your Majesty's kingdom,
there has never before been such suffering from wounds or affliction by disease."
Now, various tribes of barbarians have arrived at this place in flight.
The Princess has passed away,
and many of the ministers and officials have also died.
Therefore, these members of the monastic community should not remain within the royal realm;
it is only right that they be expelled.
On the day prior to the King’s [departure],
those who ought to drive [the horses] did not do so;
examine this matter thoroughly and in detail.
The ministers were of one mind;
they delighted in expelling the assembly of monks and informed the king of this.
He wished to expel the community of monks from the king's realm.
At that time, the resident bhikṣus within the territory of King Red-Face spoke with indignation, saying:
"If these monks are to be driven out..."
"We, too, shall not remain here.
The ministers spoke with indignation,
"You all should likewise depart as you please."
After the Princess arrived in the Land of the Red-Faced Ones,
King Han Xingchong venerated the methods of the Daoist masters;
consequently, all the Chinese monks came to the borders of the Land of the Red-Faced Ones.
At that time, all the relics,
sacred teachings, sutras, śāstras, articles of worship, and permanent assets belonging to the monastic community of that realm within the country of Carmukha were [seized].
Carrying all these with them,
they proceeded to the great kingdom of Gandhāra in the west. At that time,
In the lands of Han, China, the country of the Red-Faced Brahmans, Khotan, and so forth, as far as the Ganges River,
the Semblance Dharma will perish and leave nothing remaining.
On the other bank of the Ganges, in the country of Kūśāmbī, the Semblance Dharma shall remain in the world for three months.
Finally, it was extinguished.
The entire assembly proceeded to the seashore where the Naga King Elapatra dwells within the realm of Gandhara.
By the power of the Triple Gem.
As the waves surged upon that sea,
the Dragon King reflected:
"For what reason do the waves surge at my dwelling place?"
With his divine eye, he observed that the Semblance Dharma of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s holy teaching was nearing its extinction, and beheld the final period for seeing the Saṃgha;
he then transformed his own body into that of an old man.
Emerging from the sea,
he paid homage to that assembly of monks and questioned them, saying:
"From where have these monks come?
Where are they going?
The monks replied:
"We originally resided within the borders of the Crimson-Faced Kingdom.
Our patrons lacked faith and destroyed the permanent endowments and the vihāras."
Therefore, we went to the kingdom of Mahāgaṇḍhāra.
The Nāga King asked:
"The community of monks is extremely vast."
"What provisions do you have?
After traveling for more than forty days around the sea toward the great country of Kāñcanapura,
they finally arrived there.
"The monastic community currently has only twenty days' worth of provisions.
How shall we reach that place?
When the monastics heard this, they were concerned.
They all wept aloud.
Upon seeing this, the Dragon King was overcome with extreme grief and distress.
He said to the assembly of monks,
"Here is a direct path;
there is also a bridge made of snakes."
"Those who are able to go upward shall quickly reach that place.
Having spoken these words,
the old man vanished from sight.
Then that dragon king manifested a path leading up the mountain;
transforming his own body into a great serpent,
he formed a bridge across the sea.
He reflected thus:
"If I were to ordain this assembly of monks now,
my previous evil karma would [be activated]."
Now that you have received the body of an animal,
you may yet attain liberation;
thus you should make this vow.
The snake-bridge remained in place for more than fifteen days,
and many people and animals passed over it.
While people and animals were crossing the snake-bridge, [the following occurred].
Some even fell into the water and died.
Because such humans and animals came and went back and forth,
the snake’s back was split open and destroyed.
Blood flowed like rain,
and the ocean turned to blood.
A great multitude of monks crossed over by way of the Snake Bridge.
At that time, the remaining red-faced obstructors did not let him pass;
subsequently, the great serpent fell into the ocean and, having ended his life,
was reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
The ocean also dried up.
At that time, the community of monks arrived at the kingdom of Gandhāra;
the king of that country prepared all the necessary offerings.
For two years they made offerings so that each might be at peace and happy.
When the two years had passed,
that king relinquished his life.
The king had two sons;
one believed in the Buddha-dharma,
while the other practiced the teachings of the non-Buddhists.
Later, there was a struggle for the throne.
At that time, because the monastic community had acted as a proxy for Prince Śraddhā,
he achieved victory and subsequently succeeded to the royal throne.
During that king's reign,
he provided the Saṃgha with full provisions for their livelihood and requisites;
after six months had passed, [he continued to do so].
There was a bhikṣu who killed that king and succeeded him to the royal throne.
The entire populace of the kingdom of Gandhāra rose up at once and killed the Bhikṣu King,
and they drove out all the remaining members of the Saṃgha.
Upon exiting the King’s realm,
the Semblance Dharma also perished in the kingdom of Gandhāra;
the entire monastic community was scattered and driven into exile.
Previously, when he was in other lands, at such a time,
the kings of the West, the kings of the North, King Yavāna, and others possessed greater merit and fortune than before.
These three kings formed a league as one family.
At that time, those three kings governed the western and northern regions.
Then, each of those three kings led a hundred thousand troops to attack the kingdom of Kaśmīra.
The king had annihilated three hundred thousand soldiers along with their king, leaving not a single one remaining.
At that time, the King of Kūśāmbī, desiring to repent for and eliminate the sin of having killed such a multitude of soldiers, [acted as follows].
He summoned all the monks within the realm of Jambudvīpa to the kingdom of Kuśinagara; subsequently,
the various images engaged in mutual strife within it.
Consequently, they slaughtered one another until not a single survivor remained;
thus, the Buddha’s image-dharma (śāsana) in Jambudvīpa was extinguished from this point forward.
Each detail is explained extensively as set forth in the *Candragarbhabodhisattvavyākaraṇa-sūtra*.
Fifty-seven koṭis and six nayutas of years after the parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
the World-Honored One Maitreya will appear in the Sahā world to transform and guide sentient beings.
One Scroll: The Causes and Conditions for the Extinction of the Semblance Dharma of Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
